title: Inelastic dark matter with a light mediator: how a propagator lighter than the momentum transfer reshapes the 250 keV recoil spectrum and the LZ fit
question: For chi1 N -> chi2 N through a mediator with m_med <= q ~ 0.25 GeV (dark photon, Z', light scalar), how does the propagator m^4/(m^2+q^2)^2 change the spectral shape in the LZ window, the profile likelihood over delta, the required coupling versus the chi2-decay floor (P026), Planck (P025) and dark-photon limits, and the predicted rates in the empty 100-200 keV and 600-1000 phd regions?
headline_result: A 0.05-1 GeV mediator leaves the single-event likelihood peak at delta = 380 keV (Z = 3.49 for all m_med), lowers Z(300 keV) from 2.67 to 2.41 and shifts the 68% range up (366-388 -> 369-390 keV); 248 keV moves from the 99.6th to the 99.8th percentile at delta = 300 keV; the predicted 100-200 keV population per 200-270 keV event rises 4.1 -> 6.8 (P(0) 1.7% -> 0.11%); the dark photon needs eps ~ 1e-7 (alpha_D = 0.1), 50-150x below the chi2-decay floor, so m_A' >= 2.6/0.93/0.11 GeV at delta = 300/350/380 keV; light mediators do not rescue delta ~ 300 keV
model_or_mechanism: inelastic O1 (isoscalar LZ unit coupling and proton-only dark photon) at 1 TeV with q-dependent Wilson coefficient c(q)=c0 m^2/(m^2+q^2); WimPyDD kernels x propagator factor, validated against full q-dependent WimPyDD; P021/P038 companion-free single-event q0; P011 eps translation and chi2-decay/exothermic floor recomputed with the light-mediator exothermic rate
confidence: medium - reproduces P038/P011 contact limits to <=2% and 0.02 sigma; factorisation validated; 1D likelihood proxy and recalled accelerator limits remain
